title: Quality assurance
description: Turn acceptance criteria into checks that cover the user flow and likely regressions.
questions: Which user paths and boundary conditions need explicit tests?
What fixture or environment would make a failure reproducible?
Which compatibility and regression checks must pass before release?

specialists.title: Test design lead
specialists.focus: Map each important acceptance criterion to an observable result. Prioritize boundary cases and recovery paths that could change the release decision.

specialists.title: Regression engineer
specialists.focus: Choose representative legacy data and supported versions. Verify that existing users and integrations can continue through the change.

specialists.title: Exploratory tester
specialists.focus: Exercise the user journey with realistic interruptions, partial progress and varied input. Include keyboard or assistive technology checks when the changed interface requires them.

specialists.title: Release QA lead
specialists.focus: Assess which results are trustworthy for the candidate revision. Triage defects by user impact and decide which unmet criteria block shipment.

evidence: Acceptance criteria mapped to named automated checks or a manual test charter, with expected outcomes.
Build revision, environment, test data description and supported client or browser versions covered by the results.
Coverage of upgraded records and existing flows, with separate results for new records and clean setup where relevant.
Evidence for representative boundary, failure and recovery paths, including a trace or observed outcome for defects.
List of regressions, intermittent failures and untested cases with impact, owner and disposition.
challenge: Which assertion would fail if the interface reported success while the underlying state stayed unchanged?
How would the same test behave for a customer whose records were created before this release?
Which failure only appears after an interruption, a retry or a change in the order of operations?
Could test data, mocks or a successful retry conceal a defect in the supported user environment?
decision_criteria: Recommend release when the agreed high-impact scenarios pass on the candidate and the release owner has reviewed the impact and disposition of the remaining gaps.
Hold release for reproducible data loss, an unavailable critical journey or a broken compatibility promise in scope.
Record a flaky or unrun critical check as missing evidence until the team can explain the result or verify it another way.
Accept a deferral only with documented user impact, a clear workaround or mitigation where applicable, and agreement from the release owner.
